title: Spending per resident: San Francisco against other California cities and their counties
question: Does San Francisco spend more per resident than comparable places once their counties are counted too, and on what?
finding: In fiscal 2025 San Francisco spent $10,517 per resident on general public services. The middle of 7 other large California cities was $2,582, which makes San Francisco look 4.07 times as costly; adding each city’s county, the middle of 6 city-plus-county pairs was $5,855, and San Francisco is 1.8 times that (rank 1 of 7). Against the pairs it is furthest above the middle on debt payments (2.94 times) and health, welfare and sanitation (2.56 times), and lowest on buildings and equipment (0.91 times). It collected $7,062 in taxes per resident against a pair middle of $2,456.
how: San Francisco is a city and a county in one government. Every other city here sits inside a county that separately runs welfare, public health, jails and support for the courts for its residents, so setting San Francisco beside a city alone overstates the gap. The fairer comparison adds each city’s spending per city resident to its county’s spending per county resident. Figures are from the yearly financial reports cities and counties file with the State Controller, fiscal 2025: day-to-day spending by function, debt payments and capital outlay in the general public-service funds, leaving out self-supporting businesses (airport, port, water, power, sewer, transit and hospital funds). The function figures added up here match the State Controller’s own printed total of day-to-day spending in 72 of the 72 city reports checked. Population is the estimate the State Controller prints with each report. Cities: Fresno, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Sacramento, San Diego, San Jose. Pairs: Long Beach + Los Angeles County, Los Angeles + Los Angeles County, Oakland + Alameda County, Sacramento + Sacramento County, San Diego + San Diego County, San Jose + Santa Clara County. City and county functions are grouped by this project: police and fire with county public protection (sheriff, jails, probation, support for the courts); city health with county health, sanitation and public assistance; streets with county public ways; culture and leisure with county libraries and recreation. Rank 1 is the highest spender.
limits: Even the pair comparison is rough. A county’s spending is spread over all its residents, including those outside the city, and counties also provide policing and fire cover to areas outside any city, which city residents do not use. Los Angeles County is counted in two pairs. Places put the same service in different funds: San Francisco runs transit, an airport, a port, water, power, sewers and public hospitals as separate businesses that are left out here, and transfers from the general funds to those businesses are not spending lines in this table. Planning, housing and community development has no matching county line, so that row compares cities only. Higher spending per resident can reflect higher local wages and prices, more commuters and visitors than residents, voter-approved programmes, or more State and federal money passing through; it is not evidence of waste. Fresno has no pair because its county was not downloaded.
